title: 5a-3: tree-structured ParseResult
description:
## Parent

sutra/30 (PRD: core model redesign)

## What to build

Rework ExtractedSymbol to carry children directly instead of using parent_qualified_name for containment. Adapters produce a tree of symbols. Pipeline flattens the tree for DB insertion, assigning parent_symbol_id during a depth-first walk.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ExtractedSymbol gains children: Vec<ExtractedSymbol> field
- [ ] parent_qualified_name: Option<String> removed from ExtractedSymbol
- [ ] RustAdapter and DartAdapter produce tree-structured output (methods nested under impl blocks, functions under modules, etc.)
- [ ] Pipeline tree-to-flat conversion: depth-first walk assigns parent_symbol_id during DB insertion
- [ ] Round-trip test: tree output flattened and inserted, queried back, matches expected parent-child structure
- [ ] Edge case: top-level symbols have no parent; deeply nested symbols maintain full chain
- [ ] Behavioral parity: same symbols in DB with correct parent_symbol_id as before

## Blocked by

- sutra/31 (LanguageAdapter trait + registry)"

messages.text: Codex adversarial review: **approve**. No ship-blocking findings. Parser tests passed in sandbox; pipeline integration tests (17/17) verified separately. DFS insertion correctly threads parent_id, resolver reconstruction stays flat (correct for its consumers), container type coverage is symmetric across Rust and Dart parsers. Risk score 0.604 driven by churn/complexity — convention violations are pre-existing pipeline symbols, not from this change.
